decisive_items: A PET scan showed an intensely fludeoxyglucose-avid focus in the left anterior pelvis at the junction of the left and rectosigmoid colon, strongly suspicious for malignancy
new soft tissue thickening in the ascending colon near the cecum suggestive of a mass
response.rationale: The PET-avid rectosigmoid focus and prior ascending colon mass are strongly suspicious for colorectal cancer, whereas the diffuse colonic thickening and elevated calprotectin are nonspecific inflammatory findings that do not override the malignancy signal.

rejected.why: Diverticulitis was only a possible prior CT suggestion at the descending–sigmoid junction; the intensely FDG-avid rectosigmoid focus and ascending colon mass make malignancy more likely.

Ulcerative colitis could explain diffuse colonic inflammation and high calprotectin, but it does not account for the intensely FDG-avid rectosigmoid focus or the prior ascending colon mass suggestive of malignancy.
